transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I… I’ve been feeling unsettled at work. Some of the staff emails and morning announcements at school feel like they’re… about me, like there’s a message in them. My colleagues say they’re sent to everyone, and I know that, but I can’t quite shake the feeling.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people can't hear?

Sometimes… yes. Not all the time. When the house is quiet, or after my classroom empties, I’ll hear a woman’s voice say my name, or make a little comment about what I’m doing. It’s clear enough that I answer, and then… I realize no one’s there.
Do you ever find it hard to express your thoughts or feel like your thoughts are disjointed or don't make sense to others?
I don’t think so… not really. I mean, I sometimes lose my thread if I’m tired, but I haven’t noticed my thoughts not making sense to people.
Have you noticed any changes in your behavior or daily routines that seem unusual or out of character for you?

A little, yes. At school I sometimes… get stuck on odd things. Like during a lesson or an art-fair meeting, I’ll stop what I’m doing to line up markers or papers in a certain way. And sometimes I repeat a phrase someone just said instead of answering properly. It’s embarrassing, because it interrupts things.
Do you believe the emails and morning announcements actually contain hidden messages about you?

I… yes. I know it sounds unlikely, and people at school have pointed out the emails go to everyone. But I still can’t shake the feeling that some of them, and the morning announcements, are… meant to say something about me. Coded, I suppose.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are racing or jumping from one idea to another in a way that's hard to follow?
Not really, no. I can get distracted, but I wouldn’t say my thoughts race or jump around in a way I can’t follow.
Have you noticed doing things in a very unusual or abnormal way that doesn't seem to have a reason?

Yes… I suppose so. Mostly at school. I’ll stop in the middle of something and start arranging markers or papers in a very specific pattern, for no real reason. Or I’ll repeat what someone just said instead of answering them. It’s… embarrassing, and it gets in the way.
Do you find yourself doing things over and over, like checking or cleaning, that you feel you can't control?
Not really. I mean, I might check something once or twice like anyone, but I don’t feel driven to clean or check over and over like I can’t stop.
Do you ever have trouble putting your thoughts into words, so that others have a hard time understanding what you're trying to say?
I don’t think so. I mean, sometimes I pause or choose my words carefully, but people usually understand me well enough.
Do you often have difficulty organizing your thoughts or activities?

Sometimes, yes. In lessons or meetings, I’ll sort of stop what I’m doing and get stuck arranging markers or papers just so. Or I’ll repeat someone’s words instead of answering. It’s not constant, but it does interrupt things… and I feel embarrassed.
Do you believe that the messages you think are hidden in the emails and announcements are meant to be understood by you alone, or could others understand them as well?

I… I suppose I think they’re meant for me, mostly. My colleagues say the emails go to everyone, and I can see that, but certain phrases in them feel like they’re about me in a way others wouldn’t pick up.
Do these feelings and experiences happen only at school or also when you're at home or in other places?

Mostly at school. It’s the staff emails and the morning announcements that set it off… like certain wording is meant for me, even if people show me it went to everyone. At home, it’s not really the same.
Have these feelings and experiences been constant since they started, or have they come and gone?
They’ve come and gone a bit, I suppose… but they’ve been around for about four months now. The worries about coded messages, and the voice I sometimes answer.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are not coherent or are difficult for others to understand when you're speaking?
I don’t think so. I mean… I’m usually careful with what I say. Maybe I get a bit tangled when I’m stressed, but I haven’t really noticed people not understanding me.
Do you often find that your thoughts are fragmented or hard to put together in a logical way?
Not often, no. I can usually put things together well enough. If I’m under pressure, I might lose my thread a bit, but… I wouldn’t say my thoughts are fragmented.
How long have you been hearing the woman's voice?
About four months, I think. Not all the time, but that’s when it started.
Have these experiences and feelings been affecting your ability to work or interact with others at school?

A bit, yes. I’m still teaching, but I’ve had to ask coworkers to cover parts of some project lessons, and planning meetings have been harder to get through without help. Outside of school… I haven’t been very reliable with book club or theater things, and some neighborhood events.
Do you feel like your thoughts are jumbled or don't make sense when you're by yourself?
Not really, no. When I’m on my own I might get distracted or go over things too much, but I wouldn’t say they don’t make sense.
Do you think your way of thinking has changed since these experiences started?

Maybe a little. I… I seem to read more into things now. Like staff emails or morning announcements at school—I get this feeling they’re sort of about me, or meant for me somehow. Even when people point out they went to everyone, it’s hard to just let it go.
Do you often give answers that are not related to the question being asked?
I don’t think so. I mean… sometimes I might take a moment to answer, but I’m usually trying to respond to what was asked.
